findings.title: Six closure scripts ran 30-34 mutants each and killed none; between them they solve 53 optimizations per gate
findings.claim: On the 36-mutant sample, optimality.py, validate.py, manual_plan.py, plan_view.py, card.mjs, solar_alignment.py exited 0 for every mutant they ran on (30, 30, 30, 34, 34, 34 runs respectively), while features.py killed 12 of 30, entities.py 3 of 37, env_drift 2 of 37.

findings.note: closures.json recorded seconds are CI seconds (~14x this box); kills are first-killer-in-cost-order, so overlap among the expensive scripts is a lower bound

findings.title: Measured closures are the transitive package import: validate.py executes 8 of its 38 closure modules
findings.claim: closures.json lists 38-44 production modules for every solver script because importing any heatpump_optimizer submodule runs the package __init__.py, which imports coordinator.py (and through it the whole integration); the scripts execute far fewer.
findings.mechanism: Caveat: 'executed' counts function bodies, so a module that matters only through import-time data (const.py for open_meteo/solar_alignment/plan_view) shows as forced although it is a real dependency; every other forced module is code the script never calls. tests/closure.py records sys.modules at exit; custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/__init__.py lines 64-77 import coordinator, thermal_model, topology, frontend, manual_plan at package import time, so `from heatpump_optimizer.optimizer import ...` in validate.py pulls in all of them. A change to a module a script never executes (e.g. away.py, narrative.py, pump_mode.py) then forces every solver script -- 2424 recorded CI seconds -- to run.
